_comment: Curated alarm-name -> citation registry read by scripts/check_alarm_citations.py (#1959). Every CloudWatch alarm that has been in ALARM >72h must have an entry here (exact AlarmName key) naming the incident row or issue that explains it, or the /wrap gate flags it by name. Since #2912 the same holds for an alarm that FIRED AND CLEARED within the last 72h (episode start and end both in-window, read from describe-alarm-history) — a flap between wraps is invisible to current-state duration by construction, so it needs an entry or an explicit --decoded line just like a standing red. Add an entry the same session a new long-red alarm (or flap) is triaged; remove/replace one once the underlying issue closes AND the alarm has actually cleared live. Since #2996 a citation that names a `#N` must name an issue that is still OPEN: the gate reads `gh issue view` for every currently-lit alarm's citation and flags a dead reference, because a citation string is not an owner (measured 2026-08-22: 4 of 7 entries pointed at closed issues, 3 of them on lit alarms). A citation with NO `#N` is never flagged by that check — a dated, self-clearing state is honestly cited in prose — but the 14-day `issueless_ancient_reds` rule still forces a `#N` past that tenure. PRUNE an entry when its alarm recovers. Since #3258 a citation may not assert a recurrence NEGATIVE ("no recurrence since", "has not recurred") unless the same note names how it was derived — the log group it was read from, or the query that read it (filter-log-events / describe-alarm-history / start-query). A recurrence-negative is unfalsifiable from the registry alone, and the measured instance hid a live recurrence for four days: this alarm's entry read "fixed by #3066/PR#3075 …, no recurrence since" while the identical finding fingerprint 539c6d sat in /aws/lambda/life-platform-qa-smoke inside the last 72h. Enforced offline against the committed file by tests/test_check_alarm_citations.py::test_the_live_registry_carries_no_underived_recurrence_negative (scripts/check_alarm_citations.py::unfalsifiable_negatives), so it runs on every PR rather than only at wrap. A POSITIVE claim needs no marker — it is checkable by looking.

ADR-133 derived the permanent $150 base FROM a measured steady state ($4.12/day = 82.4% of $150) that lands inside band 1 (73-87%), so a threshold=1 alarm fired continuously on the platform's DESIGNED steady state from 2026-08-12 (17+ consecutive days) — the same background-noise failure #1927 was filed to prevent, one band up. Band 2 (reader narratives paused) is not the designed state at ~81% MTD spend, so a full week pinned there is genuinely rare and worth answering; #1927's own amendment already moved the two CI gates out of band 1, leaving only five internal/dev features there. EXPECTED POST-DEPLOY: this alarm should clear once `cdk deploy LifePlatformMonitoring` ships the new threshold, because live BudgetTier has not sustained >= 2 for a full week. Re-read the live CloudWatch alarm state after that deploy — if it has NOT cleared, that is new information (tier has been at 2+ longer than assumed here) and this entry should stay with an updated note; if it HAS cleared, prune this entry once it has been OK longer than the #2912 72h flap window.

qa-smoke-warnings.note: FIX LANDED 2026-08-27 (#3258, epic #2578) — awaiting deploy + one clean nightly. Cause, derived from /aws/lambda/life-platform-qa-smoke (filter-log-events over 30d, pattern "[QA] DETAIL"): the ONLY non-[chronic] reader-truth WARN driving this alarm was finding 539c6d on `/`, severity low, whose own 576-char note ends "This is ambiguous rather than contradictory — the phrasing is acceptable for describing a cycle objective. No flag warranted on reconsideration." The judge retracted its own finding and the pipeline counted it. Two structural reasons, both now fixed: (1) reader_truth_qa.assess_prose consulted the ruling ledger only under `severity != "low"`, so a finding the model itself rated low was never adjudicated — `is_vagueness_objection` (#3003) returns True on this exact note; (2) all five advisory rulings (#2959 x2, #3003, #3199 x2) said "visible as advisory, never gating" but expressed it as severity=low, and low increments the alarmed WarnCount — there was no channel below it. The adjudication is now a FIELD on the finding (`rulings`) and qa_check_reader_truth routes it to the non-alarmed ChronicWarnCount as `reader_truth:advisory`; WarnCount now counts exactly the findings no reconsideration fired on. NOT phrase-matched: `_WITHDRAWAL_RE` was deliberately NOT extended with "no flag warranted" (the #2959/#3003/#3199 family has failed in the field three times); tests/test_reader_truth_retracted_3258.py replays the recorded payload and asserts the phrase list did not grow. EXPECTED CLEAR: within ~24-48h of the qa-smoke Lambda redeploy (the alarm's 86400s Maximum window has to roll off a WarnCount=1 datapoint). PRUNE this entry once the alarm has been OK for longer than the 72h flap window, per the weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat rule above. IF IT DOES NOT CLEAR: re-derive from the log rather than from this note — the residue #3258 names honestly is that a retraction NO ledger predicate adjudicates still reaches WarnCount, and the durable fix for that (a per-finding `verdict: flag|withdrawn` response field) is unshipped because it cannot be measured without a live Bedrock invoke.

weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat.citation: arming transition of the #2820 dead-man 2026-08-21 — not a delivery failure
weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat.note: Kept 2026-08-22 (#2996). The alarm is OK, but #2912's flap check reads a 72h window and this alarm's only episode is inside it: describe-alarm-history shows INSUFFICIENT_DATA -> ALARM at 2026-08-21 20:44 PT and ALARM -> OK at 21:44 PT — one hour, immediately after #2820 deployed the WeeklySignalSent dead-man (treat_missing=BREACHING, so a freshly created alarm with no datapoints is ALARM by construction until the first one lands). No signal was missed. THE PRUNE RULE, corrected: remove a recovered alarm's entry once it has been OK for longer than the flap window (72h), not the moment it clears — pruning on recovery alone trades a stale entry for a flap-gate red, which is what happened while writing this. Prune after 2026-08-24 21:44 PT if still OK.
